_说明: 见证者点击气泡台词文件：格式=对象 {_说明, lines}，lines=字符串数组（句子池，句数不限）。
第二关宋代语境：晷与主角相认后性格放开，俏皮灵动、偶带文绉绉雅趣；文本不绑定任何具体外貌与服饰，通用适配所有皮肤形象。
抽取与播放归 Y5 波（洗牌袋整轮不重复；池空/缺文件不弹+告警）。
英文字段（2026-11-01 增补）：可选「lines_en」（与 lines 逐条等长、按句一一对应）；lines_en 缺失或缺省时回退显示中文 lines，既有中文字段一律不动。
lines: 看腻我现在这副模样了？衣橱就在边上，这回随你怎么换，可别挑花了眼哦。
宋人的木头，讲究‘三分规矩，七分风雅’。慢慢瞧，心急可磨不出严丝合缝的好榫卯。
使一使‘锐眼’嘛！瞧瞧哪儿该让、哪儿该合。别硬怼，木头也是有脾气和性子的。
啧，方才那一下削得真利落！我瞧着，当年的手艺至少找回来两成了。
子曰：‘工欲善其事……’哎呀，背这些酸文作甚！总之一回生二回熟，多试两次就合上了。
《营造法式》里规矩千万条，但早在几百年前，就全化作你骨子里的直觉了。信自己的手，错不了。
手酸了就歇会儿，我给你捶捶肩～不过，茶水可得你自己倒。
这宋代的构件，一层叠一层，叫斗栱。别看它玲珑小巧，整座大殿的万钧飞檐，全凭它稳稳托着呢。
怎么样，脑海里有没有浮现出点什么？是当年的雕梁画栋，还是咱们曾一起乘凉的飞檐？
榫卯相咬，阴阳互生，木石无言，千载不朽……咳咳，如何？我念得可有几分雅致气韵？
别光死盯着一个面看，把它转一转——你心里想它怎么转，它在掌心里就怎么动。
你琢磨榫卯归琢磨，刨花和木屑可别往我这边吹啊，咳咳……弄得我满身都是！
天赋值攒够了没？够了就去衣橱里多开几件新衣裳，我好几个模样可都眼巴巴盼着出来透气呢。
千年前的工匠一根铁钉都不用，就能起万丈高楼；你当年也是这般厉害，自然难不倒你！
别急嘛，木头有木头的规矩，慢慢琢磨，它自然会为你让出路来。
你尽管放手去试，错了大不了重来。有我在边上看着你呢，慌什么。
lines_en: Tired of this look of mine? The Wardrobe is right over there—this time, change me however you like. Just don't get lost choosing.
Song craftsmen held wood to “three parts rule, seven parts grace.” Take your time—impatience never polished a seam-perfect joint.
Give the Keen Eye a try! See where the wood should yield and where it should meet. Don't force it—wood has its temper too.
Tsk, that was a clean cut! By my eye, you've recovered at least a fifth of your old craft.
Confucius said: “If a workman would do his work well...”—oh, why recite musty classics! Bottom line: the first time is strange, the second familiar—try a couple more and it will fit.
The Yingzao Fashi holds a thousand rules, but centuries ago they all sank into your bones as instinct. Trust your own hands—they won't betray you.
Rest if your arms ache—I'll rub your shoulders~ Though the tea, you'll pour yourself.
This Song member, layer upon layer, is called dougong. Small and delicate as it looks, the whole hall's ten-thousand-weight flying eaves rest squarely upon it.
Well? Has anything surfaced in your mind? Carved beams and painted rafters of old—or the eaves we once sat beneath, enjoying the shade?
Tenon bites mortise, yin and yang beget each other; wood and stone keep silence, unfailing a thousand years... ahem. Well? Did I recite that with a proper air of elegance?
Don't fix your eyes on one face—turn it about. However you will it to turn in your mind, it moves so in your palm.
Ponder your joinery by all means, but keep the shavings and sawdust off me, cough, cough... I'm covered in it!
Saved up enough Talent yet? Then open a few more new outfits in the Wardrobe—several of my looks are longing to come out for a breath of air.
A thousand years ago, craftsmen raised towering halls without one iron nail; you were every bit as good back then—this won't stump you!
No hurry—wood has its own rules. Study it slowly, and it will make way for you.
Try as boldly as you like—if you err, you simply begin again. I'm right here watching you. What is there to fear?
